Capstone: Flood Protection & Storm Drainage — Marsa Alam

Supervised by five faculty members. Protects the Port Ghalib masterplan on the Red Sea coast from 100-year flash floods.

Rainfall analysis→Watershed delineation→HEC-HMS hydrographs→Structures design→HEC-RAS 2D check→SewerGEMS network

1 · Meteorological study

Frequency analysis of annual maxima from Marsa Alam and Ras Binas stations in HYFRAN (Gamma fit), then IDF/DDF curves. Design storm: SCS Type II, 79.10 mm for 100 years.

2 · Morphology & runoff

Automatic delineation in GIS; Tc by three-segment slope method; SCS Curve Number per catchment; pre- and post-development models in HEC-HMS.

3 · Hydraulic design

Trapezoidal lined channels (Manning, FlowMaster), RC-box culverts with riprap aprons, a 10 m embankment dam and a detention pond, all for T = 100 yr.

4 · Verification

HEC-RAS 2D in three stages: pre-development, post-development without structures, post-development with structures, including culvert 2D connections.

5 · Urban storm drainage

Catch basins, street gutters and manhole spacing; network sized in SewerGEMS against slope, velocity and minimum-diameter criteria.

6 · Alternatives study

Two drainage schemes compared. Scheme 1 selected because it sends less flow, debris and sediment into the marina, reducing dredging.
